rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient to locate the eight-peak elution window and identify critical separations while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Keep the gradient fixed and raise temperature to test whether temperature-dependent selectivity breaks up the central cluster and the nearly coeluting final pair. The short initial elution window leaves ample room for later slope refinement.

Halve the gradient slope at the more promising temperature to test whether the remaining close pairs separate through increased retention and altered gradient selectivity. The current last peak at 5.08 minutes gives room to improve resolution before incurring a time penalty.

The 20-minute gradient is nearly fully resolved with no time penalty. Lower temperature by one grid step to adjust selectivity around the remaining critical pair while checking that the other separations retain sufficient resolution.
Return to 60 C and shorten the gradient by one step to shift the selectivity of the remaining critical pair. This tests for full resolution near the best method while bringing the last peak earlier.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to adjust gradient selectivity around the nearly resolved best method. This also slightly reduces the gradient slope, which may lift the R = 1.46 pair above threshold; monitor the other close pairs for losses.

Lower the endpoint one step to make a finer slope adjustment than a two-minute gradient change. This should improve the two early critical separations while testing whether the later R = 1.78 pair retains full resolution.

This gives a slope of 0.045 organic fraction/min, just steeper than injection 7, targeting improvement of the R = 1.49 pair while preserving the early separations. All peaks should elute before the gradient ends, making this a fine slope adjustment using valid grid settings.

Injection 8 has reached the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark. Raise the starting organic fraction one step to seek earlier elution, with the resulting shallower slope helping preserve the early critical separations; check whether the later close pair remains resolved.

Reduce the slope from 0.040 to 0.0375 organic fraction/min to improve the early R = 1.08 separation while testing the available margin in the later R = 1.78 pair. Injection 8 remains the maximum-score fallback as we seek a faster fully resolved method.

Test a lower-temperature selectivity regime at the higher starting organic fraction, since slope adjustments alone have not fully resolved this faster elution window. The earlier temperature comparison suggests possible elution-order changes, so assess the entire separation pattern while retaining injection 8 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Probe below the apparent temperature-driven coelutions at 50 C to see whether reordered peaks yield a second fully resolved selectivity regime. Keep the gradient fixed to isolate temperature effects; injection 8 already secures the maximum CRF.

Test the low-temperature boundary to move away from the central near-coelution seen at 35 C and assess the reordered late peaks. The last peak at 8.44 minutes leaves some room for increased retention without a time penalty.
Shorten the newly fully resolved low-temperature gradient by one step to reduce elution time. Check whether its critical R = 1.73 and R = 1.89 separations remain above 1.5 as the gradient steepens.

Return to the fully resolved low-temperature slope while shifting the organic window upward by 0.05 to accelerate elution. This tests whether a stronger starting solvent can shorten the separation without the resolution loss caused by steepening the gradient.

Test a substantially steeper gradient for a faster separation after a possible central-pair elution-order reversal, rather than continuing small changes toward coelution. Monitor all pairs, especially the late separation, while retaining injection 8 as the proven maximum-score method.

Test a stronger starting solvent with a shallower slope to retain the fast elution window while improving the late critical pair. The starting-solvent shift may also widen the reversed central separation seen in injection 16; injection 8 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Shift the organic window upward one step while preserving injection 17’s slope to seek earlier elution and improve the remaining R = 1.35 central separation. Check that the late R = 1.67 pair and the increasingly early peaks remain fully resolved.
Injection 18 is now the fastest fully resolved method tested. Shorten its gradient by one step to seek further time savings, checking whether the R = 1.61 and R = 1.65 pairs retain full resolution.

The steeper gradient lost resolution, so test a stronger starting solvent combined with a shallower slope to accelerate elution while restoring separation. Injection 18 remains the fastest proven fully resolved method; watch for central-pair order changes at this higher starting organic fraction.

Reduce the slope at the stronger starting solvent to recover the sole unresolved pair from injection 20. This tests whether its central separation can reach R ≥ 1.5 before the last peak becomes slower than injection 18’s 4.14 minutes.

Return to the fastest fully resolved gradient and raise temperature by one step to test further acceleration through temperature-dependent selectivity. Monitor the late close pair particularly carefully; injection 18 remains the fully resolved fallback.

Return to 25 C and test a slope between the fully resolved injection 18 and the faster but unresolved injection 19. Raising the endpoint one step provides a smaller acceleration than shortening tG by two minutes, locating the resolution boundary more closely.

Test whether a stronger starting solvent moves the central critical pair past its coelution region into a faster, reordered separation, using injection 18’s successful slope. This is an exploratory acceleration; injection 18 remains the fastest proven maximum-CRF method.

Use the final injection to shorten the programmed gradient while preserving injection 18’s fully resolving slope of 0.05 organic fraction/min. All eight peaks should elute before the endpoint reaches the outlet, retaining the maximum CRF and approximately 4.14-minute last-peak time without repeating a method.
